definitions.meaning: The molecule that stores genetic instructions as a sequence of bases, organised into genes on chromosomes.
A length of DNA that codes for one polypeptide chain.
One of the alternative forms of a gene, found at the same locus on homologous chromosomes.
The alleles an organism carries for a gene, such as AA, Aa or aa.
The observable trait an organism shows, produced by its genotype and environment.
An allele that shows in the phenotype whenever it is present, even in a heterozygote.
An allele that shows in the phenotype only when no dominant allele is present.
A change in the DNA base sequence; most mutations are neutral, some are harmful, and a rare few are beneficial.

mechanismSteps: Central dogma: DNA makes protein: DNA is transcribed into mRNA in the nucleus, and the mRNA is translated into a polypeptide at a ribosome.
Monohybrid cross: the 3:1 ratio: Aa x Aa gives genotypes 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa in the Punnett square, which group into phenotypes in the ratio 3:1.
Dihybrid cross: 9:3:3:1: two genes on different chromosomes assort independently, so sixteen boxes give four phenotype classes in the ratio 9:3:3:1.
Sex-linked inheritance: a gene on the X chromosome is passed from a carrier mother to half her sons, who show the trait because the Y cannot mask it.
A common mistake: mutations are always harmful: most sequence changes are neutral because the protein still does its job, so harm is the exception, not the rule.
objectives: Describe the central dogma and predict offspring ratios for monohybrid, dihybrid and sex-linked crosses
Evaluate claims about mutations, distinguishing neutral, harmful and beneficial changes

trap.explanation: Mutation sounds like damage. Most mutations are neutral: only some are harmful, and a rare few are the raw material of evolution. In the animation a mutated gene still builds a working protein with the same job: the sequence changed, but nothing that matters did - which is why the blanket claim fails.

workedExample: In scene s2, a monohybrid cross Aa x Aa fills four Punnett boxes - AA, Aa, Aa, aa - so the genotype ratio is 1:2:1 while the phenotype ratio is 3:1, because both AA and Aa show the dominant trait. The same square gives each probability directly: 1 in 4 affected (aa), 1 in 2 a carrier (Aa), and 3 in 4 showing the dominant phenotype.
